title: Why Does Fire Burn as a Sphere in Space?
summary: Discover why zero-gravity combustion eliminates natural buoyancy convection, creating serene spherical flames where molecular diffusion dictates life and death.

sections.heading: The Force That Shapes Candle Flames
sections.content: On Earth, when you light a candle, hot air expands and becomes less dense than the surrounding cold air. Gravity pulls the denser cold air downward, forcing the hot air to rise. This buoyant natural convection pulls fresh oxygen into the base and stretches the flame into a teardrop shape.
sections.suggested_question: Why do microgravity flames form a sphere?
source_links: NASA Glenn Research Center Drop Tower Archives

sections.heading: The Freefall Revolution
sections.content: In microgravity aboard the ISS, gravity is cancelled by orbital freefall. Hot combustion gases no longer rise. Without buoyancy, oxygen cannot be pulled into the flame base by convection. Instead, oxygen must slowly migrate into the reaction zone purely via molecular diffusion.
sections.suggested_question: How does molecular diffusion replace convection in orbit?

sections.heading: Suffocation and the Life-Support Paradox
sections.content: Because oxygen moves so slowly without convection, a zero-gravity flame in completely stagnant air quickly suffocates in its own carbon dioxide shell. However, the gentle breeze from spacecraft life-support ventilation (0.05 to 0.20 m/s) sweeps the CO2 away and feeds the flame fresh oxidizer.
sections.suggested_question: What did Saffire discover about spacecraft ventilation?

title: Fire from Space vs Fire in Space
summary: Bridging NASA Earthdata satellite thermal anomaly detection of terrestrial wildfires with microgravity combustion inside the Cygnus spacecraft.

earthdata_context.application: Active Fire Detection & Burned Area Mapping

sections.heading: Planetary Heat Signatures
sections.content: From 700 kilometers above Earth, NASA satellites monitor our planet's fiery metabolism. Sensors on MODIS and VIIRS detect middle-infrared emissions, pinpointing active wildfire fronts in near real-time through the FIRMS system.
sections.suggested_question: How does NASA detect wildfires from orbit?
source_links: NASA Earthdata FIRMS Data User Guide

sections.heading: The Enclosed Cygnus Chamber
sections.content: While satellites gaze downward at continent-scale fires, engineers inside the Cygnus vehicle after ISS unberthing ignited the largest deliberate fires ever conducted in space. Here, the challenge is microscopic containment rather than planetary observation.
sections.suggested_question: Why did NASA burn Cygnus spacecraft after departing ISS?
